newsitem.title: FINLAND: Raisio has no more details on J&J deal.
newsitem.headline: Raisio has no more details on J&J deal.

text.p: Finnish food group Raisio and Johnson & Johnson will not give details on the financial terms of their U.S. deal on Raisio's Benecol stanol ester fat product, Raisio said on Wednesday.
"We have agreed not to give those details," Raisio spokesman Sten von Hellens told Reuters by telephone ahead of meetings with analysts and portfolio managers in London.

Raisio said on Tuesday it had given Johnson & Johnson company McNeil sole rights to use its Benecol stanol ester for a variety of products in North America, and said McNeil would participate in developing the product.
Von Hellens added the group would also give no details on the possible volume of its planned Benecol output in the U.S., where it plans to open a stanol ester plant.
"You can deduce something if you compare the U.S. population to the Finnish," he said, but did not elaborate.
The U.S. population is some 70 times Finland's five million and the market for Raisio's Benecol margarine in Finland is worth some 90 million markka per year, Raisio said on Tuesday.
A pre-engineering study for the plant is due to be completed in September and decisions on how big a plant and where it would be built would follow in the autumn, Von Hellens said.
Stanol ester, made from forest industry by-product plant sterol, lowers cholesterol levels. Raisio produces it in fat-soluble form.
